text:
Nick DeSimone is the kind of defenseman whose value hides from the box score. Undrafted, 31, and a free agent who worked his way up, he has no points through 9 games with Utah on 13.7 minutes a night.

What he does well shows up elsewhere. At five on five, the Mammoth have held 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey had him at 0.9 wins above replacement last season, 76th among 215 defensemen with 500 minutes, mostly from even-strength defense: opponents got 0.16 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on, 89th percentile.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small 9 game sample, shows a split game. He carries the puck in on half his entries, and carry-ins led to a chance 25% of the time against 8% for dump-ins. But only 26% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes.

Utah has had a rough few weeks, and his on-ice goals have trailed the chances. That is a reason for patience, not concern.
